Hello. Like the wise people who have left comments before me have already said 'if you like the Sniper Elite series, then you will like this new version'. I agree with that. Yes, it is sort of a new DLC but it's a big one (~90 GB), so that is something. The graphics look sharper and better to my eye. Starting over is a drag but I get to revisit some of my stealthier techniques again, so that is good. Still the bugs, though. Guys hanging around in mid-air, mid-floor, mid-vehicles after they have been shot. The stuttery stairs still makes me dizzy. 
Is it worth the $$$ - only you can decide. Is it worth the 10+ hour download? Only you can decide. We'll see how the season pass shakes out - better stuff or more of the same. And Rebellion,  please stop with the rifle skins and the other cosmetic stuff and focus on better weapons and better campaigns. That is why we buy your game.

While I enjoyed the past SE titles this is as much repitition I can take from a franchise. Aside from the skill points and weapon customization that aren't really needed to make it through the game even on high difficulty and invasion which is more of a gimick once you made it through coop/singleplayer very litte has changed since SE3 in terms of campaign gameplay. The engine while being well optimized is outdated, controls are still clunky, bots are still du.mb af and Kar/Mosin will always be the best rifles.

If you enjoy the series in general you know what you're getting into but this franchise needs some inspiration.

Also the game needs polishing. It's bugged and glitchy compared to older titles.

ON SALE ITS A YES

At $50, this feels like a cash grab honestly. Its less of a game and more of a larger DLC. 

~ 4 maps on Multiplayer - 3 for TDM, STDM, FFA and 1 for NC. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Dumb.
~Havent touched Survival or Propaganda cause I dont care about those modes
~Campaign. Meh. Hawker's voice is horrible and trash and I really cant stand listening to it lmao
~Graphics are definitely sharper I feel than SE 5. I play both on Ultra Settings across the board at 110% resolution on 3440x1440 and Resistance is a better, clearer image. Art style/Graphic style is the same as the prior entries.
**I have NOT had the performance issues that other folks have had. 3080/5800x 3d/32gb something speed ram lol/ on either NVME or SSD cant remember which lmao. Plays at 90ish to 100 FPS for myself.

~Movement is really funky at times. Sometimes the character doesnt want to go down narrow walkways or climb ladders, other times it does. Its really 'floaty'. It could be snappier and smoother
-The default controls are different than SE 5 and IDK why. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird.
~The gameplay is the same if youve played other SE titles, nothing has changed

It COULD be a good game but this was 100% a Cash Grab by Rebellion. They should have focused on SE 6 100% than this. I know it may be 2 different teams, IDK how they worked it. But ALL ATTENTION should have been placed on 6 and this should never have been made honestly. Its not bad but it is definitely not as good as the other titles are. It really should have just been sold as a DLC for SE 5 and have a lower price, $30 - $40 range. At least it wasnt $70 cause it is 100% not worth that at all.

Feels no different than Sniper Elite 5, like more of a 5.2. They played it safe but kept the same formula. It would be nice if you were able to at least start off with a better load out. Otherwise, it's fun. It's Sniper Elite. What more could you want?

What happened Rebellion? Sniper Elite 5 is still in my regular play list (I've got over 250 hours in SE5, and more in SE4), it's a great game - other than putting in non lethal, bring back S-mines! Resistance on the other hand is going to be played a lot less - the AI don't react to their close friends getting killed, or go back to passive within a few seconds, and that's on Authentic; I've only played Authentic in SE:R, no point playing lower levels as it's far too easy  - completed the first 6 levels with all stars on each in 5 hours ... 

There seem to be fewer enemy around, and the maps feel clunky and compared to SE5 and SE4. And the bugs are annoying as hell - getting stuck on top of a staircase and then thrown out of a window, trying to climb down boxes but hanging from an edge instead with legs inside the box just a few feet below, small walls that can't be climbed over, sync issues in co-op where the guest player can see enemies standing around that the host shows as dead, map sections where you fall through the terrain. 

It's like Rebellion took on some interns and gave them SE5 to mod while the real developers work on SE6. As a £10 DLC for SE5 I'd still have complaints with it, but paying full price for what is basically a buggy, part complete mod pack feels like a kick in the teeth.

This game is fun, offering the standard 9 missions like SE5, but the mechanics are basically the same as SE5. There are some bugs that I ran into while playing. I would buy SE5 rather than this game though.
campaign so short it should be a $20-30 dlc to SE5. Not a standalone game.

Let's start by saying I know my Sniper Elite games. I've played all games since the original SE2. I've noticed with every iteration the devs evolved and improved their games. But this game is something different, it feels like they have gone back.

I'll get to the cons later, so first some good things:
The graphics and visuals are awesome
The maps feel really lively
The array of weapons is different from what most people are used to and gives some refreshing brands

Well, there goes the cons:
This game, well, it feels like DLC for SE5, it's completely the same game, but with a Resistance reskin. Asking €50,- for something that feels like a DLC is just insane.
This game is far from being polishes, nothing is optimised, stairs don't work, graphics are missing, you get stuck often, which is especially frustrating when trying to be stealthy. 
Foes are getting stuck aswell, which makes them immortal.
From what I've learned about the Second World War, I've never heard of the Germans inventing wallhacks, because that's what's in this game, they can look straight through the walls at times.
Somehow my mouse disconnected from the game, but worked in menus and everything else on the PC.

Okay, time for the consensus:

It's your typical Sniper Elite, nothing too new or too fancy. It might need a few updates here and there.
I would rate this game at a 65/100.

Overall gives the usual Sniper Elite vibes. only thing with this game as of when this is being written is that there are still a few bugs and little things they need to work out, like some collision, floating objects, and I've noticed some of the enemies get stuck in some places. Overall doesn't affect the gameplay and still a good Sniper elite game so far.

Really fun. If you liked the last game, you'd 100% love this one too. I much prefer the new protagonist, you don't get many cockney accents in games. I also loved how you play as the resistance in the new mode.

The maps are tiny. this should be at best a dlc to Sniper Elite 5. it is built on the same engine and does not add anything new to the formula other than a time attack mode which itself is just a re-skin of the campaign missions to make it seem like there is more there. the gameplay is on par with the excellence of Sniper Elite 5 but its not worth $50 much less $80 if you want the inevitable dlc to what as stated should itself just be DLC for what little effort they put into designing these missions. Also there are noticeable but not game breaking graphics errors everywhere, just annoying little attention to detail stuff they clearly overlooked. if you don't already have them get Sniper Elite 5 and then 4 in that order they are both amazing games that are worth full price but don't buy this unless its at least 60% off because its only the value of a $20 game if that.

Just to point out how poorly the maps are designed. In the second mission you are tasked with recovering top secret documents that the Gestapo are allegedly frantically looking for. one of these documents is stored in a safe in an office that belongs to resistance informant. the safe is the only one in the office and we are clearly told that the Nazis know that the owner of this safe is an informant early in the mission. guess who has the key to the safe (which graphically is a combination safe not a key safe). by golly its the Gestapo agent who is casually walking around the office and who apparently has not opened the safe 10 feet away that he has a key to this entire time which is exactly where the documents he is looking for are located. This smacks of the writers and the level designers were never on the same page during development.
